To Whom It May Concern,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for vertebral augmentation (vertebroplasty/kyphoplasty) for my patient {{patient_name}}, Date of Birth {{patient_dob}}, Member ID {{member_id}}.

CLINICAL SUMMARY:
This patient presents with an acute/subacute vertebral compression fracture at [FRACTURE LEVEL], occurring approximately [WEEKS] weeks ago. MRI demonstrates bone marrow edema on STIR sequences confirming fracture acuity. The patient reports a VAS pain score of [VAS]/10 with significant functional impairment (Oswestry Disability Index: [ODI]). A [WEEKS]-week trial of conservative management including analgesics and bracing has been completed with persistent refractory pain.

GUIDELINE SUPPORT:
Vertebral augmentation is supported by multiple high-quality randomized controlled trials and society guidelines:

• VERTOS II (Klazen CA, et al. Lancet. 2010;376:1085-1092): Vertebroplasty demonstrated statistically significant pain relief compared to conservative treatment at 1 month (VAS reduction 2.6 vs 1.9, p<0.001) and maintained superiority through 12 months in patients with acute osteoporotic VCF and MRI-confirmed bone marrow edema.

• FREE Trial (Wardlaw D, et al. Lancet. 2009;373:1016-1024): Balloon kyphoplasty demonstrated significant improvement in SF-36 physical component score vs non-surgical management (p=0.0003) at 1 month, with sustained benefit at 24 months.

• ACR Appropriateness Criteria (2022): Vertebral augmentation is rated "Usually Appropriate" for acute osteoporotic VCF with MRI bone marrow edema, VAS ≥4, and failed conservative therapy.

• CMS LCD L35050: Vertebral augmentation is a covered benefit for acute VCF with MRI-confirmed bone marrow edema, significant pain, and failed conservative therapy.

MEDICAL NECESSITY:
1. Acute/subacute vertebral compression fracture confirmed on MRI with bone marrow edema
2. Refractory pain (VAS [VAS]/10) despite [WEEKS] weeks of conservative therapy
3. Significant functional impairment (ODI [ODI]) affecting activities of daily living
4. Posterior vertebral wall intact — safe anatomic candidate for vertebral augmentation
5. [Osteoporotic / Pathologic] fracture etiology

CONCLUSION:
Denial of this procedure is inconsistent with current evidence-based guidelines and will result in continued severe pain, functional decline, and risk of progressive vertebral collapse. I respectfully request immediate reconsideration and approval.

Sincerely,
{{physician_name}}, {{credentials}}
NPI: {{npi}}
